Digital ischemia

One case report describes near-complete recovery after low-level light was added to wound care and medication for procedure-related digital ischemia. The report cannot isolate the effect of light.

PBM Database summary

What the records report

One case report describes near-complete recovery after low-level light was added to wound care and medication for procedure-related digital ischemia. The report cannot isolate the effect of light.

Summary of the Evidence

One human case report was identified for digital ischemia. It describes an older patient who developed gangrene after a finger tourniquet, partial nail removal, and carbon-dioxide-laser treatment of a subungual wart. Low-level light therapy was added to wound dressings and medication. No controlled trial, animal experiment, or indication-specific laboratory study was identified. The case concerns a procedure-associated injury and should not be generalized to Raynaud phenomenon, spontaneous ischemia, or chronic peripheral arterial disease (Lueangarun and Tempark 2019).

Human and clinical evidence

The report states that skin color and digit function recovered almost completely over three months. This is a clinically relevant observation, but it is a single uncontrolled case. The patient also received dressings and medication, and there is no way to determine how much recovery was due to light, other treatment, or the natural course of the injury. A case report also cannot estimate how often the result would occur or identify which patients might benefit.

Animal evidence

No animal study directly testing PBM for digital ischemia was identified in this indication set. Findings from hindlimb ischemia or other vascular models are not direct evidence for a human finger affected by tourniquet-related injury.

In-vitro and ex-vivo evidence

No digital-ischemia-specific cell or tissue experiment was identified. The case report offers no laboratory measurements that establish a mechanism for the observed recovery.

Treatment Parameters and Generalizability

The database entry records a 633 nm wavelength, which is visible red light. The published abstract does not specify irradiance, fluence, session duration, number of treatments, or a detailed device protocol. Those missing details prevent faithful replication and make comparisons with other PBM studies difficult. The report does not include a head-to-head test of wavelengths, dose, or light versus standard wound care alone.

Interpretation

The case report describes recovery of skin color and digit function over several months after low-level light was added to wound care and medication. The observation documents what happened in one patient, but the combined treatments and absence of a control prevent attribution of recovery to PBM. Systematic case documentation and comparative studies would be needed to estimate how often similar outcomes occur and whether light changes them.

Evidence strength in source summaryVery low for recovery from digital ischemia
Publications and records1 article

Evidence strength rationale and next steps

One case report describes substantial recovery of skin color and digit function after light was added to wound care and medication. Because there was no control group and several treatments were given together, the report cannot identify the contribution of PBM. A prospective series with complete treatment details, followed by a comparison with standard care, would make the result easier to interpret.
